title: What the Reading Did Not Know

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The slate is read twice and the grain is read over once, and neither of them knows what the other cost.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the market women at the Cross, told on the first Account-day of Frost

where: Low Kiln and the Cross, Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and seventy-nine to two hundred and eighty-one days, six months and ninety-nine to one hundred and one days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing — the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the body inventoried as a wound of crust, unnamed gap, frozen thread, cold at cheek, temple and wrist and an afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; the figure read over the basket kept beside the figure paid, the told bell kept beside the heard, the stayed frost kept on its own place; the small coordinations of the hand kept on the sixth place and never promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power, a doctrine or a rule — with no present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no sixth hearing, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row question (the five askings and one further shaping stand as they stood), no tenth record-first hand, no eighth of the green or ninth of the shape, no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause, no sign, lesson, mending or payer made of the first firing of Frost, no bond changed hands, no private record opened, read or copied, and no ending. Frost 10 (Day 279) is the month's first Account-day and market and earns its own reading by its own morning light; Frost 20 (Day 289), the second, stands eight mornings beyond the close and is not brought early.
places: the flat stone by the well
the reading block under the moot-post

scenes.title: The Morning the Figure Comes
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, the chapter's only \dropcap and the first \daymark{279}{...}: Day 279, Frost 10, Tenthday, Y.H. 813, the month's first Account-day and market, the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof into the first light. Open in the small hours with the hand laid down against the fold on the one hundred and thirty-second answer as a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking, never recalled as growth, a gift, a reaching or a sign. No recap of Chapter 75; the reader has just read it. Carry 278 to 279 exact, six months and ninety-nine days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-nine days, its payer unnamed (T088). Body inventory in the old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone past the point where a child would eat it, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. He knows a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse, and wants the crust lifted two inches. Both true, the second louder in a body six months and ninety-nine days old, entered nowhere (T060/T086). Three counts in three places: the carried fire's four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, the river's water over water at the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot. Agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands (T088, T061/T082); the heard bell's four, four and a gap stays in the square beside the told bell of the Long Night and is not folded in (T078). The stayed frost lies white on the well's north lip and the plate of ice stands on its flat stone out of the path of feet, called weather and entered nowhere from Frost 8 and 9 (T083/T085 held, not paid); the dressed grain lies covered and unfigured under wool at the rack end with three readings of Smoke behind and their true subtractions locked in Berr's box (T077, T015/T041/T047). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells the coals the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, glances once at the clay jar under its lead glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, stands the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, sets the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, and gives no instruction at any hour to the basket; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs at a morning and in a basket, for neither is an opening (T058/T079, T100). Frost 10 comes on in its own morning and was not brought into Day 278; the reading is earned by this light and not anticipated. **Answer 133:** the hand goes up an inch toward the river's note, takes the small intake of the river's own going, carries it across the little silence left by one of the counted breaths in the room whose floor does not touch his, and comes down on the next low note — one house rhythm carried into a day that will be full of figures, the interval given no figure, no house count borrowed and no fifth supplied (T061/T082). Kept as an honest coordination, not a reach, hearing, seventh, payment, held change, key, power, doctrine or rule.

scenes.title: One in Twelve, As the Notice Says
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 279, no new dated heading: the first light at the Clay Yard, the half-pace to the Cross, the reading block under the moot-post, the pot board, the Slate Row fringe of the square and the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, then the carrying home at the going of the light into the small hours. **The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T015/T041/T047):** Frost's first Account-day comes to the Cross and the district's arithmetic changes for the new month and cannot be changed back. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay the smell of nothing at all, the most expensive smell in Grath; his large clean hands wipe the thumb twice before touching nothing, hold a narrow slate unopened to the forearm, pass a finger over the figure and let the eyes rest on the writing a breath longer than the writing requires, read *one in twelve, as the notice says* low into the crowd, call the levy, deny it with *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *your house*, never *I*, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon takes a hand out of a field before the dressing goes on, and go off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the first true subtraction of Frost inside, believing he has done a kindness. The printed figure stands unchallenged; a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid; the reading answers nothing for the man carried out on Day 188, the hand that went in on Seed 15 and did not come back, or the dressed grain covered under wool at the rack end, which is read over by a number that does not know what it cost and leaves the space between figure and price unsigned (T077, T098). Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies, stands half a pace off through the reading and the bell, gives no instruction or reason to the basket, and carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing. The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept in the square beside the told bell of the Long Night; its gap is not made a seventh of the full note, a fifth of the fire or an agreement with the boards' thumb-width knot, for agreeing any two would want a payer and none stands (T078, T061/T082, T088). Hessa Rale takes Berr's narrow slate up the clay road toward Greybank before noon, edge-on to her forearm, writing to her sleeve, the small flat correction of the strap and the turn of the wrist bringing the edge round, the second strap let out for the long road and the dried pale scurf of mud unbrushed on the shortened skirt, hand to slate before eyes to crowd; to a woman who asks what she carries she answers the question put and not the one behind it — *I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which* and *Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk* — and no figure comes off it; her order of reaching stays the eighth record-first hand on a place of its own, not joined to Berr's twice-wiped thumb, the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate, Ilva's strip, Marra, the charcoal or any other keeping (T080 advanced, not paid). The soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market selling over him as water goes over a stone (T090, T080). At the pot board a silent woman's sweetish green stays a colour and at the market's edge a foundling's shape stays a shape, sightings only with no eighth of either, never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, neither named, joined, given a loaf, a slate or a sale, and not promoted into a hearing, a cause or a romance (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). The stayed frost and the plate of ice are carried where the yard left them and the reading takes no figure off either (T083/T085 held, not paid); the widow's mark is untouched at a market, a road and a going of the light, because none is an opening (T058/T079). **Answer 134:** under the roof in the small hours the hand goes up an inch and takes the small intake of the heard bell's gap and the hold of one counted breath, sets them side by side with a finger between, and comes down on the river's remote note — the heard bell's gap kept beside the told and not agreed with the figure read over the basket and not made a seventh of the full note (T078, T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Firstday After
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated \daymark{280}{...}: Day 280, Frost 11, Firstday, Y.H. 813, the small hours under the Vail roof into the morning of the ordinary working day after the reading. New day, new date, no recap. Frost 11 comes on its own morning and was not brought into Day 279; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Firstday; Frost 20 (Day 289), the second Account-day, stands eight mornings ahead and is not brought early, and nothing from the reading is brought back under the roof as a lesson, a figure or a payment. Carry 279 to 280 exact, six months and one hundred days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and eighty days, its payer unnamed (T088). First smells and sounds as before: hot clay cooled under tallow, wet wool, the sour breath of the unswept corner called the thaw, the river low over lower under the finger's-width door, the kiln answering in fours with its gap and not a bell. Body inventory renewed in the old order — one crust two inches off with its unnamed gap and no third, thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; the surgeon's knowledge that a cold patient cannot clot is exact and buys nothing (T060/T086). Sella's grammar holds exactly: fire before basket, instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, The house will keep it, half-pace from every open slate, pot handle two inches out with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, fold righted without a look at his face, finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, and the widow's mark untouched at a morning, a hearth and a basket, because none is an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079, T100). The dressed grain is turned once beneath the wool for damp with a lighter touch and given no figure; it was read over yesterday by a number that did not know its cost and still does not, and the space between figure and price stays unsigned (T077). Frost's first arithmetic stays behind and unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box, the figure read still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047). Seven walked-around places are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number — the clean dark line at the Vail corner and the finer grey hairline called the thaw beside it, unswept both; the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates; the round ring where the shallow clay pan once stood with no scrape, crumb, print, chip or word; the skinned trough beside the yard well with its water called weather; the field's empty place out on the worked strips; and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, carried and not named, not paid and not joined to the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust or the dressed grain (T009/T013/T092, T098). The stayed frost lies on the well lip still and the plate of ice stands on its flat stone out of the path of feet, weather entered nowhere and no cause or payer made of it (T083/T085). Garl stays in objects and not in a story, his name unspoken two hundred and eighty days: the salt-stiff coat with the crease at the left shoulder, the wheel-seat keeping its twenty-year lean and its hollow, the clean dark line with the finer grey beside it, the tile debt against a firing neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled; no collector came up or went down the clay road for the reading and none came today (T009/T013/T092). **Answer 135:** the hand goes up an inch, takes the small intake of the river's own going and lets it go on the same note without holding, and comes down — a letting-go kept whole, not an ending made early, not a freedom and not a gift, for a freedom wants a taker and nobody under this roof has taken anything (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Count Kept in Wood
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 280, no new dated heading: afternoon at the yard well and the drying racks, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge and the back room as a direction and a sound, into the small hours at the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending the way heat goes out of a pot set off the coals and left on a cold stone; heat draws back from the fold and sits behind the pot. Inventory renewed, exact and unentered (T061/T082, T060/T086). Ilva is glimpsed once at the yard well drawing water with the pail against her knee, clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and the finer grey rack dust worked into the seam of one thumb, which she does not scrub out. Asked what the month's firings have taken now the first reading has gone up the road, her hand goes toward her sleeve and stays there; the short strip of notched birch is not taken out, read, asked about, taken a figure from or joined to the charcoal under the shelf, the cord, the knots, the pages, the tins, the missing hand or the pale line. Her eyes go to the asker and her mouth answers the question put and not the one behind it: *Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account.* She goes on with her water and nobody turns twice; the boy files no tenth record-first hand, the ninth stays nine with a finger between it and the eighth, the count stays in wood where no slate can take a figure off it, and she does not know she was read (T080 held at nine, not paid). The shallow bright patch on the flagstones is kept as it has been since Seed 22 and the broom stroke goes over it without the half-check, the stones still keeping the place where it stopped; the loft scrape lies on a place of its own and the carried man's pale line on another, not joined to it (T036/T076). Tarn at the kindling keeps six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the very lip of the sill where it cannot, with Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it and no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt; he tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, says *Yes, house* to those who want the thaw early and those who want it late, agreeing with both so thoroughly that no argument can find a foot and keeping the late because it puts off the paying though the paying stands in the ruts; the ear-sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and goes as far as the word that would call the loan before stopping, with no figure and no name — a remembered ninth stopping and no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven; the Seed 16 breath is drawn and unspent, his chest tight, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifting it, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back; his stroke goes over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check. Up in the Debt Loft, which comes to the boy only as a sound with a direction and never as a room he is taken into, the warm stone in its unmarked pot is cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiveness (T036/T076, T006, T009/T013/T092). Jorra comes through the finger's-width-open shed edge with the day's meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger, not bone-coloured slip, parts dusty forearms from clean ones as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel and a pot before any person (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*; *You'll do*), knows the full note the pot will give three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies (T035/T031/T062). The back room keeps its finger's width of open and its sound of low voices and gets no name; burned slate stands at four from Slate Row, a direction over the boards and not a fifth telling; the two tellings of the counting room shut in the war stand at two and have not become three; three sayings about a pot stand with the premature Smoke 14 note on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause; the row question stands at five askings with one further shaping and no witness under any and no row named; *he's not Vail* stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn (T065/T095, T101, T064). No sixth hearing of the full note comes and none is invented to fill the empty place. **Answer 136:** the hand takes two intakes from the room whose floor does not touch apart with a finger between and bridges them over the river's note, the bridge kept as an object on the sixth place and not a span crossed, no house count borrowed for it (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Second Morning
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated \daymark{281}{...}: Day 281, Frost 12, Secondday, Y.H. 813, the small hours under the Vail roof into the morning of the second working day after the reading. New day, new date, no recap. Frost 12 comes on its own morning and was not brought into Day 280; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Secondday; Frost 20 (Day 289), the second Account-day, stands seven mornings ahead and is not brought into a day that has not earned it, and the first reading is not looked at again as a sign, lesson, mending or payment. Carry 280 to 281 exact, six months and one hundred and one days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and eighty-one days, its payer unnamed (T088). He comes into the morning two hundred and eighty-one days old, six months and one hundred and one days, told by nobody, and the number stands exact and complete against a house that keeps its days in loaves, glances and unnamed spaces. Body inventory in the old order: one leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; the composed face that is not composure, the cold patient who will seem better before he is worse; he wants the crust lifted and cannot close two inches on the pot handle, both true and the second louder (T060/T086). Three counts in three places — the fire's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand, water over water at the door, four nails, four and a knot overhead — with no agreement among them, because agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands; the heard bell's four, four and a gap stays in the square beside the told bell and is not folded into the three (T088, T061/T082, T078). Sella's grammar holds exactly: fire before basket, instruction to fire, wool, pot, broom and running water and never to basket, The house will keep it, half-pace from every open slate, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, fold righted without a look at his face, thread left frozen, finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, one glance at the clay jar under its lead glaze and the hand shut half over nothing, and the widow's mark untouched at a morning, a hearth and a rack, because none is an opening (T058/T079, T100). The dressed grain is turned once under wool for damp with a progressively lighter touch and given no figure; the arithmetic that read over it on Frost 10 did not know what it cost and the space between figure and price has no signature (T077). Frost's first arithmetic stays locked in Berr's box up the clay road and unread under this roof, the printed one in twelve stands unchallenged and the figure read is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047). The seven walked-around places are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number, the staying frost called weather, the plate of ice standing where it was set, both entered nowhere (T083/T085, T009/T013/T092, T098 held). Garl stays in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and eighty-one days, the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled; no collector came up or went down the clay road on Frost 10, 11 or 12 (T009/T013/T092). Five askings stand on the seventh place with one further shaping and no witness; nine stoppings with no tenth; nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth unread; six hearings beside and never among with no seventh; the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth; no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T101, T036/T076, T080, T061/T082, T050/T051, T033/T034, T060/T086). **Answer 137:** the hand takes the small intake of a count from the next room, holds it past that count's letting-go and through the little silence after it, and comes down on the river's next low note, the little silence left whole and empty and not filled to make a row come out even (T061/T082).

scenes.title: Every Gap Left Gap
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 281, Frost 12, afternoon into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge and the back room as a direction and a sound, the bed, the boards and the towel. Frost 12 goes out without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming the months is set right or left wrong in so many words; no lesson was made of Frost's first reading and none is made of it now, and the next opening stands in the first firing of a later month, far off, not hoped for and not counted toward (T058/T079). Afternoon thins without ending; heat draws back from the fold; inventory renewed, exact and unentered (T060/T086, T061/T082). Stayed frost lies on the well lip past the going of the light and the yard calls it weather still, entered nowhere; the broken plate of ice stands where it was set on its flat stone out of the path of feet, clouded where the silt rose into it (T083/T085 held, not paid). Sella carries him up at the going of the light at the half-pace from every open slate, sets him on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen where it lay, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a row standing with two gaps and gives neither gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar standing cold under its lead glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and gives no instruction at any hour to the basket; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs at a going of the light, because a going of the light is not an opening (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot beside Garl's unforged sentence, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, draws the breath he does not spend, his chest tight, Ash in the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring holding what light there is; the loft stone is cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiveness (T036/T076, T006). Jorra's meal-fine grey dust, his withheld knowledge of the pot's note, his bent finger leading at the cold damper, the back room given no name, burned slate at four, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness, *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise ungiven all stand as they stood (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101, T064). In the small hours the file is turned out on the towel as instruments are turned out for a man who will never be called to use them, each thing in its own place with room between, known by its weight before the eye fell on it, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. Walk the inventory in order: six hearings with no seventh and the empty seventh place kept empty (T061/T082); the heard bell beside the told in the square, four, four and a gap, not folded into the three counts and not a seventh (T078); the three pot sayings together on their own tray and the premature Smoke 14 note on a place apart, no fourth likeness and no cause; burned slate at four from Slate Row, a direction over the boards and not a fifth telling; the two shut-room tellings at two; the ownerless question on a seventh place with five askings and one shaping, a finger between every pair, no witness under any and no row named (T101); the nine stoppings with no tenth (T036/T076); the nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth in her sleeve unread and no tenth (T080); the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth; Frost's first arithmetic locked in Berr's box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid, and dressed grain covered and unfigured under wool with the arithmetic that read over it yesterday still not knowing what it cost, the space between figure and price unsigned (T015/T041/T047, T077). Set the small dry scrape of the loft sill on a place of its own and the carried man's pale line on another, not laid across either; keep Garl in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and eighty-one days and the tile debt worse for being uncalled; keep the stayed frost, the plate of ice, the twice-and-thrice-turned grain and the week's small movements each where they were laid, with no fourth likeness standing up and no doctrine made of three (T009/T013/T092, T083/T085, T061/T082). The finding that a house keeps by not-doings stays on its own place with the boy's own gaps on another and a finger between — the two gaps above the shelf, the one crust in the fold and its unnamed empty place, the pan's gone ring, the field's empty place and the returning-line place where a hand went in and did not come out — no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T060/T086, T097 held, T098 carried). **Answer 138:** the hand takes the held interval and the empty interval from the file, sets them side by side with a finger between, and comes down on the river's next low note, neither promoted into a reach, a hearing, a gift, a keeping, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power, a doctrine or a rule; one hundred and thirty-eight filed beside one hundred and thirty-seven, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, and he makes nothing of it and will not let it stand up as a gift, because a gift wants a taker and nobody under this roof has taken anything. The hand lays back against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. Two hundred and eighty-one stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; six months and one hundred and one days are told by nobody; the fire's fifth is unpaid the same number of days with its payer unnamed. Nothing was opened, named, called, paid or ended; the file lies open on the towel with every gap left gap, every tray parted from its neighbour and nothing that had moved. Beyond the finger's-width door the frost lies white on the well lip, called weather and entered nowhere, and Frost 20 (Day 289), the month's second Account-day, stands eight mornings ahead and is not brought into this day. The river's low note goes quiet after the hand comes down.
